newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euroshares consolidate gains as Dow rallies.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euroshares consolidate gains as Dow rallies.

text.p: European bourses extended gains in afternoon trade on Thursday, buoyed by a firmer dollar and a confident start on Wall Street.

The Dow Jones industrial average opened ahead and quickly rallied 55 points to 6,866, bouncing back from Wednesday's 21-point sell-off in anticipation that good corporate results would lead the market higher.
On Tuesday the Dow rocketed 173 points, posting the second largest gain in a day in its history.
Frankfurt was comfortably higher but Paris lost early gains, accrued with the help of a weak franc and higher bonds.

London, transfixed by the country's general election next week, managed only to lurch a couple of points higher, despite encouraging inflation data which made an immediate interest rate hike after the May 1 vote less likely.

The dollar, subdued ahead of a meeting of G7 industrialised countries in Washington this weekend, remained firm against European rivals, gaining from a preliminary report that showed tame inflationary pressures in Germany.

The news lifted Germany's IBIS-DAX index, which rallied through a key level at 3,400 in late trade, also aided by the weak mark and Wall Street's open. By 1400 GMT the index had put on 1.30 percent to stand at 3,410.

Paris, before running out of steam, traded up 16 points at 2,550 for a 0.70 percent gain on the back of a weaker franc, rising bonds and a technical rally linked to the start of trading for the May stock exchange account.

Political concerns remained in the background, with investors still drawing comfort from an opinion poll on Tuesday that forecast the centre-right coalition of Prime Minister Alain Juppe would retain its majority in snap elections to be held in a matter of weeks.
London alone declined to follow the Dow's lead, trudging 5.5 points higher to 4,393.
British inflation data earlier lifted the London market, but the FTSE faces a considerable battle in advancing much further before the election.
A crucial barrier at 4,400 will prove a particular challenge, dealers said.
"The market's really kicking its heels until the election while keeping an eye on Wall Street," said BZW's head of European strategy, Richard Kersley.
March CPI, Britain's new measure of consumer price inflation, earlier showed a 1.8 percent yearly rise which strategists said would cap interest rate fears.
The prospect of a rate rise soon after the May 1 poll has dogged the London market for weeks.
"The CPI data should just cap fears of just how rates should rise," said Kleinwort Benson UK equities strategist, Philip Isherwood. "They'll go up after the election but not significantly."
European bond markets were also firm, with German bund yields widening their discount to U.S. treasuries.
STOCKS AT 1400 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 3.6 at 4391.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 1.75 at 2535.39.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 1.41 points at 3397.36. The IBIS DAX index was up 35.85 At 3402.72
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7175 against the mark versus 1.7117 in late European trade on Wednesday.
Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.10 from 126.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
GOLD fixed at $340.90, down 25 cents from the morning, trading in a narrow range in fairly quiet trade. Resistance was seen at $342.50, support at $340.00.
SILVER was steady and quiet at $4.71, down a cent.
